## Clean Inning, Clean Results

From a pitcher's perspective, there's nothing better than retiring the side in order. That's exactly what we did on October 8th—one pick, one win, no runners left on base. When you're working with a 50% probability call and it hits, you take it. Let's break down how we threw strikes all day.

## The Winning Pick: Guardians Over Sox

This was a coin-flip situation at 50% win probability, but sometimes in baseball, you trust your gut and the fundamentals. The Guardians came through, proving that even in tight matchups, the right read can deliver results. From the mound, I've learned that 50-50 games often come down to execution—and Cleveland executed.

## What Worked Today

Even money picks are always tricky. You're essentially reading the subtle advantages—bullpen depth, recent form, home-road splits. The Guardians had just enough edge to justify the call, and they delivered. That's the kind of execution that wins championships.

Just like a pitcher needs his rest days, the schedule gives us a break tomorrow. No games on the card means no picks to make. Use this time to review, reset, and get ready for the next series. In my playing days, I'd use off-days to study film and work on mechanics. Same principle applies here—analyze what worked, stay sharp, and come back stronger.

100% accuracy is a clean slate. Now we build on it.
